title: Bootstrap Model Verification Data
description: This dataset, titled Bootstrap Model Verification Data, contains the processed numerical data underlying all figures presented in the manuscript "Bootstrap Current Modeling in M3D-C1" by Saurabh Saxena, Nathaniel Ferraro, Mike Martin, Adelle Wright. The data was generated using simulations conducted using the extended-MHD code M3D-C1. These simulations include both tokamak and stellarator configurations, which were simulated with and without bootstrap current models enabled in M3D-C1. The dataset includes data files corresponding to each figure in the manuscript for the following cases, the low aspect ratio "CIRC1" tokamak case and two quasisymmetric stellarator cases (QA_Case1 and QA_Case2), and nonlinear simulations (starting with the QA_Case2 equilibrium) investigating the effects of resistivity scaling. All simulations employed self-consistent bootstrap current models based on generalized and revised Sauter formulations and the isomorphism described by landreman et al. (2022). This deposit is intended to provide full transparency and reproducibility of the figures in the associated publication, and to support further verification, comparison, or reuse in neoclassical transport modeling studies.

title: Inputs, Outputs and Plotting Scripts for paper Extending near-axis equilibria in DESC (Final Version)
description:
Python scripts and outputs from the DESC and pyQSC/pyQIC codes used to create the results in the paper "Extending near-axis equilibria in DESC". The contained README file has the details of which scripts create which figures, as well as on what versions of the codes were used. The repo also contains python pickle (.p) files and .txt files with the data used to create each figure (which are used by the plotting scripts).

This is a revision of an earlier dataset (https://doi.org/10.34770/tf2m-vq11) to be consistent with the final version of the published paper.

title: Dataset for "Stability and Characteristics of Lower-Hybrid Drift Waves: Dependence on Electron Beta and Cross-Field Relative Drift"
description: The dataset associated with this study consists of numerical solutions of the local linear dispersion relation for lower-hybrid drift waves and derived quasi-linear saturation estimates. It includes computed wave frequencies, growth rates, propagation angles, and characteristic wavenumbers over a two-dimensional parameter space spanned by electron beta and normalized perpendicular electron drift velocity (normalized to the ion sound speed). These data are used to generate five figures in the manuscript: (1) benchmark comparisons between classical and electromagnetic formulations of the dispersion relation, (2) two-dimensional stability maps illustrating the transition from electrostatic to electromagnetic regimes, (3) parameter scans identifying the dominant control parameters for LHDW stability, (4) maps of the most unstable mode properties as functions of electron beta and normalized perpendicular electron drift velocity, and (5) quasi-linear estimates of saturation properties, including normalized electric and magnetic energy fractions, field amplitudes, and polarization ratios. All quantities are derived from self-consistent linear solutions and post-processed using the same reference plasma parameters described in the manuscript.

title: Data for "Multi-Diagnostic Characterization of Laser-Produced Tin Plasmas for EUV Lithography"
description:

The files include the EUV emission spectroscopy data used to create Fig. 3 [tif], Thomson scattering data used to create Figs. 4--8 [tif], and Interferometry data used to create Figs. 9--12 [tif].
All provided files contain raw .tif data, which were processed to generate the final figures as detailed in the main manuscript. To  visualize the contrast differences in these raw images, we recommend opening them in ImageJ or similar image analysis software.

The simulations include fully nonlinear turbulence simulations with the stella and GX codes, as well as simulations of secondary modes using stella.

title: Data for "Molecular dynamics simulations of reflection and sputtering behavior of boron under deuterium ion irradiation"
description: This repository provides the data used in the figures included in the article "Molecular dynamics simulations of reflection and sputtering behavior of boron under deuterium ion irradiation,” published in the Journal of Nuclear Materials in 2026. In this work, simulations were performed on systems with deuterium projectiles impacting boron surfaces at a variety of energy ranges (10-150 eV) and angles (0-85° with respect to surface normal). These simulations were carried out using various atomic modeling tools, such as density functional theory, molecular dynamics with reactive force field potentials, and binary collision approximation. The resulting data, compiled in this repository, includes inter-atomic potential energy, reflection coefficients and chemical and physical sputtering yields.

title: Data for IMAS-based framework for NIMROD MHD data interoperability
description: This dataset contains IMAS-formatted outputs generated from NIMROD extended-MHD simulations of DIII-D discharge 163518. The collection includes equilibrium, core and edge profile information, and 3D MHD fields represented on GGD-based grids, enabling standardized analysis, visualization, and exchange of nonlinear plasma simulation results. The dataset was produced to support reproducible integrated-modeling workflows, cross-code interoperability, and downstream analysis using IMAS-compatible tools.

Gyrokinetic simulation results are compared with numerical solutions to the dispersion relations for geodesic extended modes derived in the article.

title: Data for "Development of flash lithium evaporators for NSTX-U wall conditioning"
description:
This dataset contains manuscript source files, figures, bibliography files, analysis scripts, and supporting plotting products associated with the development of flash lithium evaporators for lithium wall conditioning on LTX, LTX-beta, and NSTX-U. The files document evaporator design evolution, lithium coverage modeling, quartz crystal microbalance measurements, run-day plasma-response analysis, impurity and surface-condition comparisons, and figures used to support the NSTX-U f-LITER design basis.

The materials include LaTeX manuscript files, REVTeX/AIP support files, generated manuscript figures, Python plotting scripts, Jupyter notebooks, representative cached metadata tables, and figure-source images. This README describes the repository contents and associated analysis materials; it is not the article abstract.

title: Date for "Dynamics of Argon Metastables in Ar-CH4 Radio Frequency Capacitively-Coupled Plasma: Real-Time Monitoring with Neural Network-Augmented Broadband Optical Emission Spectroscopy"
description:
This study maps out methane breakdown chemistry in a compact DC glow discharge using Ar-CH₄ mixes at 400 mTorr, uncovering distinct zones for cracking the molecule apart and building it back up into polymers. We leaned on laser-induced fluorescence (LIF), two-photon absorption LIF (TALIF), and optical emission spectroscopy (OES) to pinpoint absolute densities of atomic H, CH, and C₂ radicals across space.
The setup shows a super-structured reaction zone driven by funky non-local electron behavior. Methane mostly splits in the cathode sheath (under 4 mm from the cathode), where H atoms hit a max density of about 2 × 10²¹ m⁻³. Digging into the Hα line shape reveals two hot H populations: one topping out at ~110 eV (from ions bouncing off surfaces) and another at ~17.5 eV (from electron smacks).
Meanwhile, the follow-up radicals CH and C₂ ramp up farther out, right at the sheath-negative glow edge (around 4-6 mm), marking that spot as polymerization central. C₂ densities peak at ~5 × 10¹⁷ m⁻³—two full orders beefier than CH's. The whole plasma's wildly out of equilibrium: gas stays chill at ~570 K, but CH(A) emitters scream hot vibes at 3300–4700 K, pointing to a niche high-energy pathway for excitation.
Bottom line: the glow discharge's jagged energy profile keeps dissociation and polymerization neatly apart, spotlighting why short discharges rock for tweaking methane chemistry.

title: Data for "Measuring static and quasi-static non-axisymmetric magnetic fields in MAST-U"
description: This repository contains the data used to prepare the "Measuring static and quasi-static non-axisymmetric magnetic fields in MAST-U" poster presented at the 26th Topical Conference on High Temperature Plasma Diagnostics (HTPD), and submitted to the journal Review of Scientific Instruments (RSI). The files include synthetic and experimental data from the novel measurement technique deployed on the MAST-U device and the Python analysis of both sets of data, as described in the paper.

title: Results of Pfirsch-Schlüter Flow Implementation in XICS Inversion Analysis
description: The X-ray Imaging Crystal Spectrometer inversion analysis used for interpreting W7-X data has been updated to include the Pfirsch-Schlüter parallel flow and flux-surface-averaged (FSA) parallel flow in the forward model used to invert the line-integrated flow measurements into a profile of the FSA perpendicular flow. The updated radial electric field results derived from the FSA perpendicular flow are compared with the results from the original inversion, charge exchange recombination spectroscopy, and neoclassical predictions made by SFINCS. Results from forward and reverse magnetic field configurations are also compared with physical expectations.

title: Dataset for Acceleration Techniques for Predictive TRANSP Simulations for Digital-Twin Between-Shot Analysis
description: This dataset accompanies the paper “Acceleration Techniques for Predictive TRANSP Simulations for Digital-Twin Between-Shot Analysis” by A. Y. Pankin, J. Breslau, M. V. Gorelenkova, M. Scotto D’Abusco, and R. M. Churchill. It contains the numerical data and plotting scripts used to generate Figs. 1–8 of the paper. The dataset includes the experimental density-profile input used in the filtering examples, processed data for the profile-filtering figures, and TRANSP output data for the comparison of the reference and accelerated predictive simulations. Python and Gnuplot scripts are provided to reproduce the figures.

title: Data for "Fast-ion enhanced modeling of neoclassical tearing modes at DIII-D and NSTX"
description: This repository provides the data used in the figures included in the article "Fast-ion enhanced modeling of neoclassical tearing modes at DIII-D and NSTX”, published in the Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion in 2026. In this work, simulations were performed on growth rate of tearing mode instabilities at DIII-D and NSTX tokamaks. These simulations included the fast ion effect calculated using TRANSP which was previously unaccounted for. The resulting data, compiled in this repository, includes the growth rate of island width, the contribution of classical, neoclassical, and polarization current effects, compared to the measured growth rate of islands.

title: Data for "Photodiode diagnostics of low-energy neutral beam interactions in LTX-beta"
description: This dataset contains supporting files for analysis of a multi-row photodiode diagnostic used during low-energy neutral beam experiments on the LTX-beta spherical tokamak. The files include processed photodiode signal-to-noise summaries, digitized beam capture and charge-exchange cross-section data, diagnostic CAD and geometry references, analysis scripts, generated figures, bibliography files, and manuscript source files. These materials document the detector layout, viewing geometry, data-processing workflow, and derived quantities used to interpret beam-synchronous soft-x-ray, Lyman-alpha, and AXUV photodiode measurements.

title: Data for "Optimizing error field correction while minimizing peak heat fluxes in SPARC"
description: This dataset contains self-contained numerical and geometric data stored in HDF5 format to reproduce all the 2D and 3D scientific figures of the paper "Optimizing error field correction while minimizing peak heat fluxes in SPARC". It includes magnetic equilibrium profiles, error-field and correction coil scans, MAFOT footprint calculations, and HEAT 3D optical heat flux and shadow-mask surface meshes for the SPARC tokamak.

title: Data for "Assessing plasma face component thermal response to rotating 3D magnetic fields for SPARC tokamak"
description: This dataset contains the raw numerical output data used to generate each figure presented in the paper "Assessing plasma-facing component thermal response to rotating 3D magnetic fields for the SPARC tokamak" submitted to Physics of Plasma in 2026.  The data are organized by figure, with each files containing the raw outputs from simulations used to construct the figures presented in the manuscript. The data were collected from HEAT simulations of plasma-facing components subjected to heat fluxes resulting from rotating resonant magnetic perturbations (RMPs) in SPARC. The deposited outputs describe the temporal evolution of surface heat flux and temperature throughout the simulations.
